item.title: Pediatricians: A Gold Mine of Antibodies
item.description: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is so common that almost all children are infected before the age of two. There are vaccines and therapies have been developed from the antibodies produced by people who have had RSV, but they aren't effective against all the many strains of RSV. New research in China is looking at a population of people who may have a better range of antibodies- pediatricians. item.title: "Africa," But This Time It's Really Africa!
item.description: There are 54 countries in Africa (plus three disputed territories), more than any other continent. You can try memorizing them by studying a map and then picturing the map while you recite them, but that hasn't worked for me because I always miss a few. I'd probably do much better by listening to a pleasant song that recites them in rhyme. item.title: When Enslaved Africans Fled South to Freedom in Florida
item.description: In grade school, we learn that St. Augustine, founded in 1565, is the US's oldest permanent city settled by Europeans. Outside of Florida, we learned nothing about what happened after that. Florida remained a Spanish colony for centuries, constantly at odds with the British colonies to the north. item.title: What To Do With Your Big Lottery Jackpot
item.description: The odds of winning millions of dollars in a lottery are very, very small, and are only slightly improved by buying a ticket. But people do win. item.title: 200 Years Ago Today: The Last Scottish Highlander Charge
item.description: A Highland charge was a traditional Scottish battle tactic involving wedge-shaped formations of Scots running toward enemy positions. Upon reaching effective musket range, they would fire a single volley, drop their muskets, and then run at the enemy with broadswords.The last such charge was conducted two hundred years ago today in North Carolina during the American Revolutionary War. item.title: Talented Woman Can Play Two Recorders with Her Nose
item.description: Acclaimed musician haruka_2go_ can expertly play two recorders with her nose (one for each nostril) at the same time, which is two more recorders than I can manage. Her performances are precise and masterful.She usually props the second recorder on an object, such as this loaf of bread. But she also will use a raised knee and complete a performance while standing on one leg.-via The Awesomer

item.title: That Time a UFO Sighting Stopped a Nuclear Weapon
item.description: In the spring of 1967, skywatchers near Moscow saw a strange unidentified object in the sky. It looked like a crescent moon, or a big illuminated C in the sky. It happened again and again, always at the same time of day as the sun was setting. Reports got into the newspapers, and UFO hunters across the USSR flocked to Moscow to investigate- or at least see the UFO. item.title: The Dream (or Nightmare) That Built California
item.description: One thing you really did study in American history class was the California Gold Rush.
